@@ -18,7 +18,7 @@ gap left for a later package, that a reviewer may want to change.
 | L9 | **Setup is bound to the phone that paired.** Every phone that opens setup gets a setup cookie (SameSite=Strict, HttpOnly) and its own one-time pairing code. Before the owner's number is known any phone on the Wi-Fi may set up; once it is, only the phone whose code paired (or that typed the number and its code) sees or posts later steps, so another phone on the Wi-Fi can neither replace the number nor see the code-generator seed. Pairing by the card's setup code binds no phone: the reply texts a page code, and the phone that types it continues (3 tries, then a fresh code, at most 3 texts an hour). Other phones see "Setup is continuing on the phone that texted the box", and later steps show the number masked. Lost-device escape (arbitrator): the paired phone can start setup over, and any other phone can with the card's setup secret, printed as the reset secret on the recovery sheet (5 wrong tries an hour); starting over re-asks pairing, enrollment, the recovery acknowledgment and the trusted-PC choice. Setup pages are open without sign-in only until setup is done; then they redirect to status and their forms do nothing. Setup progress is persisted (`SetupStore`) without any secret; the code-generator seed stays in memory until the entered code confirms it, then goes to the vault (`Hooks.SaveCodeSeed`) and is wiped. Steps run in §8.1's order, and "this PC is trusted" is accepted only after enrollment and the recovery acknowledgment. Ethernet makes the network step a no-op. At every start where setup is not done, it is treated as done if `Hooks.AlreadySetUp` reports that Finish completed (the owner channel exists), so neither a lost state file nor a failed save after Finish reopens enrollment; an enrolled seed alone never closes setup, so a reboot mid-setup or after starting over resumes where it was. `AlreadySetUp` must read a durable marker Finish writes and answer true when in doubt; it is also asked after a failed Finish, so a Finish that fails after the owner channel exists still closes setup. Once setup is done no step changes its state (checked under the setup lock), and starting over is refused while Finish runs. The setup cookie lasts 7 days (`SetupCookieFor`) so it survives a browser restart; pairing codes beyond 8 phones evict the oldest; an enrollment checked against a seed that a restart replaced is not saved. Hooks that write to the vault or render a QR code run outside the setup lock, so the modem loop's `OfferText` never waits on them. | ONB-3, §8.1, CH-4 | `setup.go`. |
 | L10 | Pairing (ONB-6): the `sms:` link prefills `PAIR <one-time code>` to the box's number (`?&body=`, read by iOS and Android). A text `PAIR <code>` with that code or the card's setup code makes its sender the owner's number, and the box replies "AgentOS is running on [host]" from its own number. Wrong pairing texts are capped at 10 an hour, then the box is silent. Fallback: type the number, the box texts a 6-digit code (3 texts an hour, 3 tries, 15 min). The broker's modem loop calls `Server.OfferText` until an owner exists. | ONB-6, §8.1 | `OfferText`, `number`. |
 | L11 | Enrollment accepts the code for the box's current 30-second step or one either side, since the phone's clock may differ slightly. A box whose clock is minutes off fails enrollment; that is visible at once and is a hardware-time matter (§13). | ONB-3 | Learn a clock offset at enrollment. |
-| L12 | Connect AI waits only on the first-boot update (`Progress.Updated`), as ONB-4 says. An API key typed here goes to `Hooks.ConnectAPIKey` and is never kept, echoed, or logged; a device-code sign-in shows the provider's https page and code. Each connection asks once, unticked by default (CAP-9: default no), whether that provider may see private data, passed through `Hooks.SetPrivateOK`; under the box the page says that, unticked, tasks needing mail or files wait until a provider is allowed on the AI providers page (L47, REV-6). Setup finishes as soon as one provider reports connected, checked after each step and on each page load (so a device-code sign-in completed on the provider's site finishes it), and calls `Hooks.Finish` at most once, whose caller starts the owner channel and sends `AllSetText` (ONB-8): three example tasks suited to connected accounts, then "HELP for commands", within three GSM-7 segments. With no provider allowed private data, task text has no route unless it is PUBLIC (§5), so the examples are PUBLIC tasks without accounts. | ONB-3, ONB-4, ONB-8, CRED-5 | `aiKey`, `maybeFinish`. |
+| L12 | Connect AI waits only on the first-boot update (`Progress.Updated`), as ONB-4 says. An API key typed here goes to `Hooks.ConnectAPIKey` and is never kept, echoed, or logged; a device-code sign-in shows the provider's https page and code. With no provider allowed private data, task text has no route unless it is PUBLIC (§5), so the examples are PUBLIC tasks without accounts. | ONB-3, ONB-4, ONB-8, CRED-5 | `aiKey`, `maybeFinish`. |
 | L13 | Pages have no script (the vault page's photo shrink, L17, is the one exception and optional); the status page refreshes itself while the box is starting (ONB-4), and the setup page only while it waits on the update with nothing to type, so a refresh never wipes what the owner is typing. | ONB-1, ONB-4 | — |
 | L15 | **Condition for wiring (P1-7 or P2-1):** the local UI runs as its own uid and process, reaching the owner channel through a narrow socket authenticated by SO_PEERCRED, never inside agentosd, so a bug in an HTTP parser on the Wi-Fi cannot reach broker memory. The ARC-2 import test stays. The page footer and the contact card carry the box page address (card C10). | ARC-2, CH-9 | Wiring package. |
 | L14 | Not built here: the live browser view (P2-6), diff and file review, the rules page, card rotation (REC-4, which setup should offer in one line once it exists), and the DIY first-boot card page (§8.4). Each mounts on `Server` without changing it. | CH-8, REC-4, CRED-8 | Later packages. |
@@ -49,7 +49,7 @@ gap left for a later package, that a reviewer may want to change.
 | L40 | **The access point picks up a rotated Wi-Fi password (CTRL-card-rot-ap; REC-4, CH-7, ARC-1, DEV-net-h).** `APLoader.Rekey(password)` restarts a running access point with the new password: same interface and SSID, WPA3-SAE only with MFP required even if `Up` had WPA2 (CH-7). With no access point up it does nothing, since the next `Up` reads the stored password; a password `Validate` refuses, or the one in use, leaves the access point untouched. If the bring-down fails it does not come back up (DEV-net-h c); if the bring-up fails it stays down with no interface exempt, and the old password, which a rotation presumes lost, is never restored (safer choice; the spec is silent). The loader holds the running config only while the access point is up. Rests on the P2-1 loader, not landed: after a Wi-Fi commit (including a 409 "card in effect") the vault process hands the new password to the root-only AP store (ARC-1), and the loader calls `Rekey` only after the commit's reply reached the phone, since the restart drops every client; the done page tells the phone to rejoin with the new card. Follow-up issue CTRL-card-rot-ap-2. While any interface's BringDown last failed, `Rekey` returns an error naming it instead of nil, even for the password in use, and `Up` refuses that interface as well as every other, because hostapd may still run there with the old password (CTRL-card-rot-ap-3, #1193); a `Down` that succeeds clears it. | REC-4, CH-7, ARC-1 | `aploader.go`, `aprekey_test.go`, `apexempt_test.go`. |
 | L41 | **Real setup progress and the page's setup (P2-2w c4; ONB-3, ONB-4, CH-12; Security L6, L8.4).** agentosd's setup mode counts the box online when `/proc/net/route` or `/proc/net/ipv6_route` holds an up, non-reject default route on an interface other than `lo`; the access point's subnet has none through the box. Online is phase `ready` with `Updated` set: the first-boot update (UPD-3) is not wired into setup mode, so `Updated` follows `Online` and AI waits for an uplink. Offline is phase `offline`, and setup continues. When the last join answered `saved` and no uplink followed for 90 s, progress sets `never_online` (a `joined` answer or any uplink clears it), and every setup step shows a fixed note: before pairing it asks the owner to check the Wi-Fi name and password and join again, or plug in Ethernet, and the number step shows the network form; after pairing it names Ethernet only. The note does not block setup, because a single-radio box answers `saved` for every join until its station device exists (c3 r4, P2-1), so such a box shows the note through setup. With no networks listed (until c4b) the network step takes a typed name. `cmd/agentos-localui` gets `AgentosdSetup` over `-sock` and a `MemStore`: a page restart starts the steps over, which agentosd's newest-seed rule (L28) covers, and the page waits up to 30 s for agentosd's socket before asking whether setup is open, then exits for its unit to restart it. | ONB-3, ONB-4, CH-12, L26, L28 | `cmd/agentosd/uplink.go`, `setup.go`, `cmd/agentos-localui`. |
 | L42 | **The card step and the claim in the page (CTRL-card-sock, #1115; HW-1, HW-10, F10, ARC-2).** With `-vault-sock` and setup open, `cmd/agentos-localui` runs `firstboot.Begin` over `CardBox`: the claim state is a `change.FileStore` at `-claim-state` (`claim.StatePath`), the card latch one at `-card-latch`, the reset is `/card/reset` and the provision is `/card/provision` on a background context with a 2-minute limit (as L38). An owned box skips Begin, since its reset could remove a vault in use; with no `-vault-sock` there is no card step and agentosd's finish stays held (card pending, fail closed). The display and `Hold()` stay in the page (ARC-2: agentosd links no card code); `CardFinish` reports `page_setup_card{confirmed:true}` to agentosd before each finish, and agentosd latches the report for the process. A provision refused with reason `codes_unconfirmed` (egress K21) or a reset answering `remade` sets `CodesVoid`: setup marks step 3 not done, shows the replace-the-old-entry note on the codes step until a new code confirms, and answers the refused confirm with 303 to `/setup`; the display keeps the card. The card step says a card printed before a restart is void. Residual: agentosd trusts the page's report on the page's uid alone (PeerUID), so a compromised page can report a card that was never confirmed; the vault process's own provision check is the backstop, and making the vault refuse finish's seal without a provisioned card is a later finding. The page unit cannot yet read the claim state or write the latch (its `/var/lib/agentos` is read-only, and the seller writes the state as root): a release finding for the image package. | HW-1, HW-10, F10, ARC-2, K9, egress K21, K22 | `localui/firstboot.go`, `card.go`, `setup.go`, `claim.go`, `setuphooks.go`, `cmd/agentos-localui`, `cmd/agentosd/setup.go`. |
-| L43 | **Setup's providers through agentosd (P2-2w c4e; CRED-5, CAP-9, ONB-3).** `AgentosdSetup.Providers`, `ConnectAPIKey` and `SetPrivateOK` call `page_setup_providers`, `page_setup_api_key` and `page_setup_private_ok`, which agentosd passes to the vault process (egress K23). The private-data box is unticked by default (CAP-9 default no), and the answer can be changed after setup on the AI providers page (L47). | CRED-5, CAP-9, ONB-3, CRED-1, L28 | `cmd/agentosd/setup.go`, `localsrv/setupproviders.go`. |

The private-data box is ticked by default on a plan sign-in and unticked on an API key (D-115, L12), and the answer can be changed after setup on the AI providers page (L47). | CRED-5, CAP-9, ONB-3, CRED-1, L28 | `cmd/agentosd/setup.go`, `localsrv/setupproviders.go`. |
 | L44 | **No station device means Ethernet only (P2-2w c4 r1, #1223; CH-12, ONB-3).** Until #936 gives the box a Wi-Fi station device beside the access point, every join answers `saved` and a rejoin cannot get the box online. `Config.Station` tells setup whether one exists; `cmd/agentos-localui` wires it to `StationDevice("/sys/class/net", -iface)`, which counts any interface other than the access point's with a `wireless` directory or a `phy80211` link, read again each time the page renders a never-online step so an adapter plugged in later counts. With none, the never-online note is the Ethernet-only one before pairing too, and the number step shows no rejoin form; the network step itself is unchanged, since the saved connection is what a later station device will use. An unreadable directory counts as none (Ethernet always fixes the cause; a rejoin might not). Nil `Station` keeps c4's rejoin advice. The unit's sandbox (`ProtectKernelTunables`, no `PrivateNetwork`) leaves `/sys/class/net` readable. | CH-12, ONB-3; #936 | `localui.StationDevice`, `Config.Station`, `cmd/agentos-localui` `station`; close with #936 once the image ships a station device. |
 | L45 | **The box's number and texts in setup (P2-2w c4c; CH-1, CH-12, ONB-6; §8.1 pairing).** `AgentosdSetup.BoxNumber` asks agentosd (`page_setup_line`) and answers whether the line can text, and the number when the line reports an E.164 one. While it cannot text, the number step says plainly "Pairing is not available yet: I cannot send texts right now. Reload this page to try again." instead of a number or a code, so the step never shows a pairing path that cannot work. While it can text but the SIM does not report its number (some SIMs never do), the step says "I do not know my own number yet, so you cannot text me first." and opens the number entry, which pairs by a texted code (ONB-6; UX B1 on #1269). `Send` goes through agentosd (`page_setup_send`), which sends only setup's fixed texts (`localapi.SetupText`). `PairTexts` (started by `cmd/agentos-localui`) long-polls `page_setup_inbound` and offers each PAIR text to `Server.OfferText`, texting back its reply; it stops when agentosd answers setup closed. Residuals: a reply that fails to send is not retried (the owner texts PAIR again); a PAIR text that reaches agentosd while the page's loop is down waits in agentosd's bounded inbox, but one taken by a loop that then dies is lost; the paired text's "this PC" wording is in the allow-list, so a served `HostInfo` other than that must widen `SetupText` first. | CH-1, CH-12, ONB-6 | `setuphooks.go`, `setup.go`, `pages.go`. |
 | L46 | **The committed rotation result is the confirming session's (ROT-result-bind, #1316; REC-4).** The result can carry the new code generator's otpauth seed, so `Rotation` binds it to a SHA-256 of the confirming session's token: `/rotate/card` posts go through `Rotation.serveCard`, which holds a lock across the display's handler so the provisioner knows whose post committed. `/rotate/done` shows it once to that session only; another session is sent home and the result stays for the confirmer. It expires at the vault process's confirm window (`RotationStarted.Expires`), capped at `resultTTL` (30 minutes, recovery.PendingTTL) after the start when that is later or absent. `/rotate/enroll` and `/rotate/show` clear it (on any post, matched or not), as does Start, and each bumps a generation, so a commit whose answer arrives after one of them (within the 2-minute commit limit) stores nothing. A commit reached other than through a session's post has no confirmer and its result shows to none. Rests on agentosd session tokens being per-phone and secret (the cookie is HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict). The display itself is still shown to any signed-in session while it waits (L37); that is #1338's concern, not this row's. | REC-4 | `rotwire.go`, `rotation.go`. |

diff --git a/broker/localui/privatedefault_test.go b/broker/localui/privatedefault_test.go
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..b155f7540
--- /dev/null
+++ b/broker/localui/privatedefault_test.go
@@ -0,0 +1,157 @@
+package localui
+
+import (
+	"errors"
+	"html"
+	"net/url"
+	"regexp"
+	"strings"
+	"testing"
+)
+
+// REQ: CAP-9, REV-6
+
+// setupForms returns each Connect AI form on the page, keyed by its
+// action and provider ("ai-device anthropic").
+func setupForms(t *testing.T, page string) map[string]string {
+	t.Helper()
+	forms := map[string]string{}
+	for _, m := range regexp.MustCompile(`(?s)<form method="post" action="/setup/(ai-[a-z]+)"><input type="hidden" name="provider" value="([a-z]+)">(.*?)</form>`).FindAllStringSubmatch(page, -1) {
+		forms[m[1]+" "+m[2]] = m[3]
+	}
+	return forms
+}
+
+// #1403 (D-115, §8.1 step 6): the private-content question is ticked by
+// default on a plan sign-in and unticked on an API key, and it names the
+// provider whose servers the content goes to.
+func TestThePlanSignInPreTicksPrivateContent(t *testing.T) {
+	r := newRig(t)
+	r.runSetupToAI()
+	page := html.UnescapeString(r.get("/setup"))
+	forms := setupForms(t, page)
+	plan, ok := forms["ai-device anthropic"]
+	if !ok || !strings.Contains(plan, `name="private" value="1" checked>`) {
+		t.Fatalf("plan sign-in not ticked by default:\n%s", page)
+	}
+	for _, k := range []string{"ai-key anthropic", "ai-key openai"} {
+		f, ok := forms[k]
+		if !ok || !strings.Contains(f, `name="private" value="1">`) || strings.Contains(f, "checked") {
+			t.Fatalf("%s: not asked, or ticked by default:\n%s", k, page)
+		}
+	}
+	for _, want := range []string{
+		"Let Anthropic see your private content: mail, documents, chats, and anything made from them.",
+		"Let OpenAI see your private content",
+		"Your passwords and keys are never shown to it.",
+	} {
+		if !strings.Contains(page, want) {
+			t.Fatalf("page lacks %q:\n%s", want, page)
+		}
+	}
+	// Left as it is, the plan sign-in records yes.
+	r.post("/setup/ai-device", url.Values{"provider": {"anthropic"}, "private": {"1"}})
+	if !r.hooks.private["anthropic"] {
+		t.Fatal("plan default not recorded as yes")
+	}
+}
+
+// U-4 (#1422 item 4): a refused key records no answer, and the box comes
+// back as the owner left it, so a retry does not quietly flip it.
+func TestARefusedKeyKeepsTheOwnersPrivateAnswer(t *testing.T) {
+	r := newRig(t)
+	r.runSetupToAI()
+	r.hooks.mu.Lock()

+		t.Fatal("answer recorded before the key was stored")
+	}
+	if f := setupForms(t, r.get("/setup"))["ai-key openai"]; !strings.Contains(f, `name="private" value="1" checked>`) {
+		t.Fatalf("box not as the owner left it:\n%s", f)
+	}
+	r.hooks.mu.Lock()
+	r.hooks.keyErr = nil
+	r.hooks.mu.Unlock()
+	r.post("/setup/ai-key", url.Values{"provider": {"openai"}, "key": {apiCanary}, "private": {"1"}})

+// U-5 (#1422 item 5): the providers page says tasks can't run only while
+// no connected provider may see private content.
+func TestTheProvidersIntroShowsOnlyWhenNoneIsAllowed(t *testing.T) {
+	const intro = "Tasks that need your mail or files can't run until you allow a provider that is connected."
+	r, _, fp := providerRig(t)
+	r.signIn()
+	if p := html.UnescapeString(r.get("/providers/")); !strings.Contains(p, intro) {
+		t.Fatalf("no connected provider allowed, intro missing:\n%s", p)
+	}
+	fp.mu.Lock()
+	fp.ps[0].PrivateOK = true // OpenAI, connected
+	fp.mu.Unlock()
+	if p := html.UnescapeString(r.get("/providers/")); strings.Contains(p, intro) {
+		t.Fatalf("a connected provider is allowed, intro still shown:\n%s", p)
+	}
+	fp.mu.Lock()
+	fp.ps[0].PrivateOK, fp.ps[1].PrivateOK = false, true // only the unconnected one
+	fp.mu.Unlock()
+	if p := html.UnescapeString(r.get("/providers/")); !strings.Contains(p, intro) {
+		t.Fatalf("only an unconnected provider allowed, intro missing:\n%s", p)
+	}
+}

+// R1 (#1436 review): a yes given on the plan sign-in is not undone by
+// saving a key for the same provider with the box as the page shows it.
+func TestAKeyAfterThePlanKeepsTheProvidersYes(t *testing.T) {
+	r := newRig(t)
+	r.runSetupToAI()
+	r.post("/setup/ai-device", url.Values{"provider": {"anthropic"}, "private": {"1"}})
+	if !r.hooks.private["anthropic"] {
+		t.Fatal("plan sign-in did not record yes")
+	}
+	f, ok := setupForms(t, r.get("/setup"))["ai-key anthropic"]
+	if !ok {
+		t.Fatal("no key form for the provider after its plan sign-in")
+	}
+	v := url.Values{"provider": {"anthropic"}, "key": {apiCanary}}
+	if strings.Contains(f, `name="private" value="1" checked>`) {
+		v.Set("private", "1")
+	}
+	r.post("/setup/ai-key", v)
+	if !r.hooks.private["anthropic"] {
+		t.Fatalf("saving a key undid the plan's yes; key box was:\n%s", f)
+	}
+}

+// L2 (#1436 review): a device-code start that fails, or hands back a link
+// that isn't https, records no answer, shows no link, and leaves an
+// unticked box unticked.
+func TestAFailedDeviceStartRecordsNothing(t *testing.T) {
+	for name, set := range map[string]func(*fakeHooks){
+		"error":   func(h *fakeHooks) { h.deviceErr = errors.New("provider down") },
+		"http://": func(h *fakeHooks) { h.deviceLink = "http://example.invalid/device" },
+	} {
+		t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			r := newRig(t)
+			r.runSetupToAI()
+			r.hooks.mu.Lock()
+			set(r.hooks)
+			r.hooks.mu.Unlock()
+			r.post("/setup/ai-device", url.Values{"provider": {"anthropic"}})
+			if _, ok := r.hooks.private["anthropic"]; ok {
+				t.Fatal("answer recorded for a sign-in that never started")
+			}
+			page := r.get("/setup")
+			if strings.Contains(page, "example.invalid/device") || strings.Contains(page, "WXYZ-1234") {
+				t.Fatalf("link or code shown for a failed start:\n%s", page)
+			}
+			f, ok := setupForms(t, page)["ai-device anthropic"]
+			if !ok || !strings.Contains(f, `name="private" value="1">`) || strings.Contains(f, "checked") {
+				t.Fatalf("form gone, or the owner's unticked box came back ticked:\n%s", f)
+			}
+		})
+	}
+}
